topic: probability-valid adaptive priority resampling for stochastic multi-turn rare-event search

public_evidence.source: Finke, Johansen, Lee, Murray, Resampling in conditional SMC algorithms
public_evidence.use: General properly-weighted resampling framework. Adaptive and dependent resampling schemes can remain valid when the actual resampling law and index distribution are accounted for in post-resampling weights; properly weighted persistent SMC retains an unbiased normalizing-constant estimator. The paper also gives counterexamples showing unbiasedness alone does not imply acceptable variance.

public_evidence.source: Paige, Wood, Doucet, Teh, Asynchronous Anytime Sequential Monte Carlo
public_evidence.use: Particle Cascade precedent: asynchronous local offspring decisions and bounded live memory can retain unbiased marginal-likelihood estimation. Its theorem uses randomized particle ordering/arrival assumptions and does not by itself license deterministic semantic best-first priority expansion.

public_evidence.source: Owen and Zhou, Safe and Effective Importance Sampling
public_evidence.use: Defensive mixture/control-variate precedent for protecting importance sampling against severe variance increases. Its specific variance guarantee depends on the control-variate construction and is not automatically inherited by the simple defensive mixture derived here.

public_evidence.source: Angell et al., Estimating Tail Risks in Language Model Output Distributions
public_evidence.use: LLM-specific importance-sampling evidence: unsafe proposal models match brute-force tail-risk estimates with roughly 10-20x fewer samples; harmful-output probabilities around 1e-4 can be estimated with about 500 samples. This is proposal-based rare-event estimation, not sparse high-fidelity evaluator correction.

derived_design.name: randomized_priority_resampling_with_defensive_floor
derived_design.iid_descendant_correction: for M iid descendant slots with ancestor A_m ~ q, assign post-resampling weight W_{A_m}/(M q_{A_m}) before subsequent transition/likelihood factors
derived_design.transition_guard: if the environment/tool transition is itself proposed from Q rather than the base transition P, multiply the separate transition likelihood ratio P/Q; resampling correction alone is insufficient

toy_variance_stress.interpretation: Proper weighting preserves expectation, but a poor priority score can increase variance despite the defensive support floor. Proposal-quality/second-moment monitoring and fallback toward epsilon=1 are therefore efficiency guards distinct from correctness.

deterministic_pruning_stress.meaning: If a deterministic top-score rule gives proposal probability zero to excluded branches and the estimator only reweights retained support, target failure mass on excluded branches is irrecoverable.
deterministic_pruning_stress.scope: Toy support-loss diagnostic, not a universal bias formula for every estimator or recovery scheme.

scope_and_negative_evidence: Finke et al. validates properly weighted adaptive/complex resampling, but does not imply that an arbitrary deterministic score-priority queue is unbiased without explicit selection probabilities and correction weights.

Particle Cascade proves an asynchronous anytime construction under its own randomized-order assumptions; its scheduling mechanism is not evidence for deterministic BOA-style semantic best-first selection.
The defensive floor is a support and weight-ratio guard, not a guarantee of variance improvement. In the toy, sufficiently noisy priority scores are worse than base multinomial sampling.

If tool/environment dynamics are biased or replayed from a law different from the deployment/base law, exact transition likelihood ratios may be unavailable; in that case an unrestricted base-risk claim is not justified by branch-resampling weights alone.

The LLM tail-risk paper demonstrates proposal-model importance sampling, but this pass did not find an agent/LLM-specific method with explicit sparse higher-fidelity evaluator correction and measured high-fidelity-call savings.
next_tests: Find a sequentially valid method to adapt epsilon and/or the priority proposal from past particles while preserving proper weighting, then add a variance/second-moment gate that falls back toward base resampling when measured gain disappears.

Map dependent sibling selection and random particle counts into the general properly-weighted framework; separate what is proved from the paper's statement that random particle counts can be handled by state-space extension.
Test whether Owen-Zhou-style mixture control variates can give a sequential analogue of a best-component variance guard for base-plus-priority proposals.
Continue searching for agent/LLM multifidelity rare-event evaluation with sparse high-fidelity target correction, not merely proposal enrichment.
